methodology.unit: public official job posting or official role index
methodology.counting_rule: Record observable role families, locations, and requirements; do not estimate market size or preserve volatile search-result totals as a trend metric.
limitations: The sample is deliberately small and first-party; it is not a census of FDE hiring.
A listed job location does not prove the location of every customer engagement.
A requirement on one regional posting is not generalized to other regions unless another source supports it.
A removed posting proves only that the page is no longer available, not that a role family has disappeared.

signals: The public index separates FDE, forward-deployed software engineering, and technical deployment leadership.
The checked index visibly separates general roles from healthcare and semiconductor variants while the live set continues to change.
The same official search result can change quickly, so this snapshot records role presence rather than treating a headline total as a market metric.
observations.scope_note: One employer's public index; useful for observing role-family structure, not total market demand.

signals: The posting requires spoken and written Japanese and English.
Travel is expected mainly within Japan.
Success is tied to production adoption, measurable workflow impact, and eval-driven product feedback.
observations.scope_note: The bilingual and domestic-travel requirements apply to this Tokyo posting, not automatically to every role in Japan or Asia.

signals: Production artifacts explicitly include MCP servers, sub-agents, and agent skills.
The role combines discovery, production LLM engineering, evaluation, enterprise deployment, and reusable pattern capture.
The posting estimates customer-site travel at 25 percent, depending on location.
observations.scope_note: A single US multi-location posting from one AI lab.

signals: The role centers high-quality data infrastructure, customer and operator systems, and low-turnaround delivery.
Large-scale processing, distributed systems, full-stack delivery, and rapid experimentation remain explicit signals.
observations.scope_note: A US posting in a data-engine business; it should not be generalized to every AI FDE role.

signals: The posting explicitly separates a Next.js-focused profile from an AI-builder profile.
Production agents, MCP servers, migrations, code audits, performance work, and customer enablement coexist in one role family.
observations.scope_note: A US professional-services posting with employer-specific product depth.

signals: The role focuses risk, audit, and compliance workflows with customers across Europe and the United States.
Golden datasets, regression infrastructure, tracing, guardrails, and judgment about whether a workflow needs an agent are explicit requirements.
observations.scope_note: One London-based vertical SaaS posting; customer footprint is not the same as job-location demand.

observed_signals: The sample contains distinct core-platform, data-infrastructure, migration, AI-builder, vertical, and deployment-leadership roles.
Several postings make customer-facing production delivery and reusable field learning explicit rather than treating them as post-sales support.
candidate_implications: Choose a primary engineering spine instead of presenting as a generic AI generalist.
Prepare evidence for hands-on production delivery, adoption, and product feedback in addition to model knowledge.
geography_views.limitations: The sample is concentrated in US technology employers and does not represent all North American industries or cities.

observed_signals: The sampled London role combines regulated workflows, agent reliability, customer trust, and cross-region customer travel.
candidate_implications: For a regulated vertical role, show how evidence, explainability, human responsibility, and regression control become system behavior.
geography_views.limitations: This quarter has one Europe-based official posting in the structured sample; it supports a role example, not a Europe-wide pattern.

observed_signals: The official index shows Tokyo and Seoul role presence.
The Tokyo posting explicitly requires Japanese-English bilingual work and mainly domestic travel while keeping the same end-to-end production and adoption mandate.
candidate_implications: Treat local-language discovery and cross-language technical communication as demonstrable delivery skills when the posting requires them.
Do not replace engineering evidence with cultural familiarity; the sampled role still requires full-stack production delivery.
geography_views.limitations: The detailed regional requirement comes from one Tokyo posting. No claim is made about every employer in Japan, Korea, or East Asia.

observed_signals: The sampled official index also lists roles in Singapore, Sydney, and Abu Dhabi.
candidate_implications: Read the live posting for language, travel, work authorization, and customer-footprint requirements rather than transferring assumptions from a US role.
geography_views.limitations: Presence in one employer index is the only supported conclusion; the sample is too thin for regional capability comparisons.
